sections.overall: Redemption '26 will most likely be remembered as a "filler" PPV. No huge gains or losses, with three title changes which should have been better matches, given the talent involved. The best match of the event, and the week, was Kyle Fletcher vs Bandido (8.86), as predicted. Hopefully the next month's build of storylines will create enough intrigue for All In at the end of August. A tricky week overall.
sections.mens: Kevin Knight sandwiched the week,  in two title matches: his main event at Redemption loss to Kenny Omega (8.51) and successful defense to Darby Allin in the opener on Dynamite. Surprisingly fun, thanks to the No Holds Barred gimmick, was Chris Jericho vs Tommaso Ciampa. Little else to shout about, despite there being so many matches this week.
sections.womens: Two new champions: Willow Nightingale defeating Thekla (7.32) and Maya World gets her first taste of gold with her win over Hikaru Shida (5.55) for the Women's World and TBS Titles respectively. Neither were great matches and did not do the talent involved justice. A missed opportunity and both title changes questionable.
sections.menstag: The Young Bucks vs Moxley & Ospreay (7.62) underdelivered in all honesty. Especially when you look at all four men's recent lofty PPV standards. Cage & Copeland held their titles in a forgettable match. And the Double Chain match turned out to be a disappointment. A far from stellar week.
sections.womenstag: On Dynamite, Divine Dominion and Sisters Of Sin pulled of a fun No DQ match (6.2) Both teams had a modest gain from this.
sections.trios: After several weeks of no Trios matches, we were given two - both on Collision. Unfortunately, neither were particularly strong nor led to sizable gains. The champs - Cassidy, O'Reilly & Strong - successfully defended their titles and have another title match confirmed for Dynamite.
